title: QBench vs LabWare: Which LIMS Is Right for Your Lab?
summary: Compare QBench vs LabWare across LIMS, pricing, compliance, integrations, automation, deployment, and scalability to choose the right platform for your lab.
body_markdown:
## **TL;DR**


- QBench is a cloud-based LIMS focused on configurable workflows, sample management, QMS, inventory, reporting, customer portals, and transparent tiered pricing.
- LabWare is an established enterprise laboratory informatics platform combining LIMS, ELN, sample management, instrument integration, automation, and regulated laboratory workflows.
- QBench emphasizes no-code configuration and cloud deployment, while LabWare supports complex enterprise workflows and multiple deployment approaches.
- The right choice depends on laboratory complexity, compliance requirements, IT resources, integrations, implementation scope, and long-term scalability.


When comparing **QBench vs LabWare** , laboratories are evaluating two LIMS platforms with different approaches to configuration, deployment, implementation, and enterprise laboratory management.


QBench focuses on a cloud-first LIMS experience with no-code workflows, automation, customer portals, inventory, QMS, and published pricing. LabWare provides a broader enterprise informatics environment built around mature LIMS capabilities, integrated ELN functionality, instrument connectivity, and highly configurable laboratory processes.

## **QBench vs LabWare at a Glance**


### **What Is QBench?**


[QBench](https://www.scispot.com/blog/qbench-review) is a cloud-based LIMS designed to manage samples, testing workflows, reporting, inventory, equipment, customer interactions, and quality processes.


Its capabilities include:


- Sample and test management
- No-code workflow automation
- Worksheets and calculations
- Inventory management
- Customer portals
- QMS and CAPA
- Equipment management
- APIs and instrument integrations
- Billing and reporting


QBench also publishes its pricing. Current plans begin at $16,500 per year for five users, with higher tiers adding inventory, integrations, QMS, equipment management, and advanced analytics.


### **What Is LabWare?**


[LabWare](https://www.scispot.com/blog/labware-review) is an enterprise LIMS and laboratory informatics platform used across pharmaceutical, biopharma, clinical, environmental, food, manufacturing, and testing laboratories.


LabWare supports:


- LIMS
- Integrated ELN
- Sample and lot management
- Stability workflows
- Instrument interfacing
- Inventory management
- Compliance reporting
- Dashboards and analytics
- Enterprise system integrations


Its integrated ELN can access LIMS data directly, allowing experimental and operational laboratory information to remain connected.

## **QBench vs LabWare Feature Comparison**


### **Sample Management and Workflow Automation**


QBench supports orders, samples, tests, batches, projects, protocols, worksheets, automated calculations, approvals, barcode labels, and configurable automation rules. Its no-code tools are designed to let laboratory teams adjust workflows without building custom software.


LabWare supports sample tracking, testing, result capture, lot management, scheduling, compliance reporting, and complex laboratory workflows across multiple industries.


Need sample workflows that can evolve with your lab? Scispot connects sample management, automation, and scientific data through itsconfigurable LIMS software.


### **Instrument Integrations**


LabWare has extensive instrument and enterprise integration capabilities. Its integration platform supports direct, file-based, database, API, REST, JSON, XML, ASTM, HL7, CSV, and other connectivity approaches.


QBench offers file-parser instrument integrations, APIs, and managed custom integrations depending on the pricing tier selected.

### **Compliance and Quality Management**


QBench's higher-tier offering includes equipment management, CAPA, document control, training records, issues, logs, and audit capabilities.


LabWare supports regulated laboratory workflows with electronic records, auditability, sample traceability, integrated ELN functionality, and compliance reporting. Its LIMS is used in environments working under requirements such as 21 CFR Part 11, ISO 17025, EU Annex 11, and CLIA.


### **Pricing and Implementation**


Pricing transparency is one of the clearest differences.


QBench publishes annual subscription pricing and separate starting costs for integrations, training, and professional services.


LabWare does not publish standard commercial pricing on its main LIMS pages. Buyers should request a complete implementation proposal covering software, configuration, integrations, migration, validation, training, support, and internal staffing requirements.

## **Which Labs Should Consider QBench or LabWare?**


### **Testing and Growing Laboratories**


QBench may appeal to testing laboratories seeking cloud deployment, published pricing, customer portals, billing, QMS, inventory, and configurable workflows within one system.


Its structure can also suit growing laboratories that want internal teams to make workflow changes through no-code tools.


### **Enterprise and Highly Regulated Laboratories**


LabWare is commonly used by organizations with complex workflows, large laboratory networks, extensive instrument estates, and demanding integration requirements. Its breadth across LIMS, ELN, instrumentation, and enterprise connectivity makes it relevant to large pharmaceutical, manufacturing, environmental, and analytical testing environments.
